messages:
nina: Noticing a packing hole in prod-sa-east1 — lots of tiny inference pods Pending while several nodes show ~0.5 GPU free. Started ~20m ago. :thinking:
omar: Grafana cluster/gpu_pending_count is 64, warmpool/util at 16%. nodes with free_fraction: 4 nodes @~0.5 each.
felix: Any recent scheduler or node-label changes? We rolled a new "slot-cohort" labeler yesterday but I thought it scoped to training racks.
sai: I saw that agent finish too. It added label `slot_cohort=isolated` and also the taint `gpu:isolate=training:NoSchedule` to some nodes. There might be a scoping bug.
infa-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-sa-east1 threshold breached (count=64) at 1965004300
omar: Can you paste a `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending` snippet?
nina: Pasted (trimmed):
```
# kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending
mini-rerank-11      Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
embed-lite-5        Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector
```
felix: That first line screams taint mismatch. If many tiny deployments don't tolerate `gpu:isolate`, they'll be blocked even though nodes have fractional free GPU.
sai: Autoscaler logs show it tried to scale but hit spot supply failures; quota fine. cloud-ops reported spot flakiness for that region earlier today.
omar: Short-term mitigations: 1) add toleration for `gpu:isolate=training` to tiny deployments (fast) 2) enable per-workload fractional coalesce in scheduler for tiny only 3) revert the taint agent scoping until we patch.
nina: I patched one deployment as a canary:
```
kubectl patch deploy mini-rerank -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu:isolate","operator":"Equal","value":"training","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
ops-bot: Patch applied to mini-rerank by nina at 1965004335.
felix: After canary, pending dropped from 64 -> 18 in ~6m and warmpool util rose from 16% -> 51%. We did see a small cost blip for that rack (~5%) but it stabilized.
sai: Risk: mixing tiny inference on previously isolated racks could impact training jobs if they spike. We should monitor NVLink and inter-GPU bandwidth.
omar: Long-term actions (infra-scheduler backlog): - tighten labeler selector so `slot_cohort` applies only to nodes labeled `workload_bucket=training` - add per-workload coalescing whitelist (tiny/background) - add a rollout gate: block taint/label agent if pending_gpu_count > 12 for 15m - add a simulated packing check in CI that runs a lightweight binpacking simulation when label changes are proposed.
nina: I opened INFRA-2175 with a runbook stub: immediate steps: 1) patch tolerations for critical tiny deploys, 2) if spot supply persists, spin a small on-demand tiny pool in neighboring region, 3) rollback labeler if the canary shows regressions. Assigned to @felix (scheduler), @sai (cloud-ops).
infra-bot: Incident INFRA-2175 created by nina at 1965004355.
felix: I'm putting an emergency scheduler patch on the canary channel: allow_fractional_coalesce=true for pods with annotation `scheduler.alpha/coalesce=tiny-allow`. Will roll to 5% first.
omar: Also propose a conservative fallback: autoscaler should attempt cross-region fallback for non-latency-critical tiny jobs before evicting or failing them. Add `latency_class` annotation to classify.
sai: Cloud-ops: I'm chasing spot alternatives now (different families) and pre-requested a small on-demand burst as a short-term backstop. Ticket CLOUD-9571.
nina: Status at 1965004399: pending=11, warmpool util=49%. Removing pages, leaving alert on. Will post final runbook and timeline in INFRA-2175 and share a short postmortem once completed.
omar: Thanks — follow-up: add canary gate to the label agent rollout: 5% nodes, measure pending_gpu delta over 20m, abort if delta > 8. I'll open the PR. :thumbsup:
